candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — appropriate PPE and respiratory protection
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — respirator selection
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish loose-fitting PAPRs from tight-fitting respirators with respect to fit-testing requirements.

options.A: A NIOSH-approved loose-fitting PAPR with a hood or helmet appropriate for the hazard.
options.B: A surgical mask used as equivalent protection for any airborne hazard.
options.C: A tight-fitting PAPR used without fit testing.
options.D: No respiratory protection if an N95 fit test cannot be passed.

candidate.rationale: NIOSH states that loose-fitting powered air-purifying respirators (PAPRs), including loose-fitting hoods or helmets, do not require fit testing because they do not depend on a tight facial seal. Tight-fitting respirators, including tight-fitting PAPRs, do require fit testing. A is correct when the selected PAPR is appropriate for the hazard and respiratory-protection program.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Loose-fitting PAPRs do not require fit testing; tight-fitting respirators do.
candidate.source_locator: Fit Testing — Overview; PAPR — Overview/What to know
candidate.stem: A healthcare worker cannot achieve an adequate fit with a required tight-fitting respirator. Which alternative does not require fit testing?
